newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian playboy lawyer given five years for theft.
newsitem.headline: Russian playboy lawyer given five years for theft.

text.p: A Russian court on Thursday sentenced Dmitry Yakubovsky, a central figure in high-level Kremlin intrigues in the early 1990s, to five years jail for stealing old manuscripts and books valued at millions of dollars.
A judge in the St Petersburg city court also ordered the confiscation of Yakubovsky's property and ordered him to pay 29 million roubles ($5,500) of court costs.

Yakubovsky, a playboy lawyer and businessman in his early 30s, featured in the power struggle in 1993 between President Boris Yeltsin and his Vice-President Alexander Rutskoi, backed by Yeltsin's opponents in parliament.

Yakubovsky, who had fled Russia after taking part in a number of business deals in the early 1990s, was secretly flown to Moscow in 1993 in the middle of Yeltsin's battle with his conservative political foes.
Yeltsin's aides wanted Yakubovsky, who had close connections with many top figures in the Kremlin, to discredit Rutskoi by accusing him of corruption.

However Yakubovsky's revelations made no difference to the outcome of the political struggle, which was finally decided in Yeltsin's favour in October 1993 when the president crushed an uprising in Moscow by his opponents.
Rutskoi was later cleared of all wrongdoing.

During his trial Yakubovsky denied any connection with the theft in 1994 of ancient Chinese, Mongolian and Tibetan manuscripts worth more than $100 million from the Russian National Library of St Petersburg.
His aides have suggested that General Dima, as he was known in Moscow's top social circles, paid the price with his arrest for knowing sensitive secrets concerning Russia's top leaders.
Yakubovsky was arrested soon after the theft in St Petersburg and has spent nearly two years in custody.
Charges against him of planning to smuggle the books and manuscripts to Israel were dropped by prosecutors.
Yakubovsky is yet to face another trial for an alleged attack on his cellmate during investigation. He has denied this charge as well.
